title: TAP Boot Profile — Auth Section
description: The reusable 'auth' section of a TAP boot profile (req-tap-auth-boot). tap_auth OWNS this fragment; the bootloader composes it rather than copying auth schema into the monolithic boot schema. It declares the external login providers, the initial-admin emails, the local-password toggle, and the admin-lockout break-glass. Secrets are NEVER here — providers reference an auth-scoped *.secret.json by key (req-tap-auth-providers-3). Boot validates this section, runs provider self-tests (live for a deploy profile), enforces the last-admin invariant, and gates on the Django deploy posture before serving.

description.description: What this auth configuration is and why (mandatory — config that grants login authority explains itself).

providers.description: External login providers configured for this instance. Multiple providers from v1 (req-tap-auth-providers-2). Empty/omitted ⇒ local password auth only.

id.description: Stable provider natural key, also the secret key by default (e.g. 'example-google', 'robco-google'). Lowercase with hyphens.

type.description: Provider type. 'google_oidc' (Google Workspace, OIDC) or 'github_oauth' (GitHub, plain OAuth 2.0 — GitHub publishes no OpenID discovery document for user login). Unknown types fail boot immediately (req-tap-auth-providers). Each type reads a DIFFERENT set of the config fields below; the allOf branches at the end of this section enforce that, so a field belonging to the other type is rejected rather than accepted and ignored.

display_name.description: Human-facing provider name on the login page (distinct from id).

description.description: What this provider is and which org/tenant it serves (mandatory per entry).

secret.description: Optional override for the auth-scoped secret key holding the client credentials. Defaults to the provider id.

critical_for_boot.description: true (default): a failed live self-test fails a deploy boot. false: an unavailable upstream logs loudly and that provider's login is unavailable, but boot continues. A malformed static config / missing secret fails boot regardless.

auto_provision.description: true (default): a permitted new login auto-creates a TAP user (with no groups). false: only pre-existing linked users may log in.

allowed_domains.description: google_oidc: Workspace domains permitted to log in, enforced via the returned hd claim (req-tap-auth-google-oidc). Required and non-empty — there is no 'any Google account' login.

allowed_emails.description: google_oidc: optional allowlist of individual verified emails within allowed_domains (e.g. pin an example.com provider to a single operator). Absent/empty ⇒ domain-only.

email_domain_fallback.description: google_oidc: match the verified-email domain when no hd is returned (consumer accounts). OFF by default; Workspace/customer providers require a returned hd. email_verified is still required when on.

server_url.description: google_oidc: OIDC issuer base URL. Defaults to Google (https://accounts.google.com). NOT available for github_oauth — allauth's GitHub adapter reads its GITHUB_URL at class-definition time, so a GitHub Enterprise Server base URL is process-global and cannot be expressed per provider entry.

allowed_logins.description: github_oauth: GitHub logins permitted to log in, matched case-insensitively (req-tap-auth-github-oauth). An authorization filter re-checked on EVERY login, never an identity key — identity is the numeric user id, because a login can be renamed by its owner and re-registered by someone else.

allowed_user_ids.description: github_oauth: GitHub NUMERIC user ids permitted to log in. The rename-proof form and the one to prefer when the account is known: a user id is immutable and never reissued, so an allowlist written this way cannot be defeated by a handle change.

owner_only.description: github_oauth: permit only the account that created this instance. The owner's value is DERIVED at boot from the environment (TAP_AUTH_INSTANCE_OWNER), never written here, so a single-operator standup declares the intent without hardcoding a handle in committed config. When declared against an unresolvable owner the provider's self-test FAILs and every login is refused (policy_unresolvable) — a declared policy with no value denies, it never degrades to allow-anyone.

allOf.description: google_oidc reads the domain/email policy and the OIDC issuer; the GitHub allowlist fields are not its vocabulary and must not be accepted-then-ignored (a config that exists and does nothing is worse than one that is rejected).

github_oauth reads the account allowlist and requires at least one clause of it — there is no 'any GitHub account' login, the same rule as google_oidc's mandatory allowed_domains. The Google-only fields are refused.

initial_admins.description: Verified emails granted tap_admin on first login (req-tap-auth-boot). Add/update-only — a typo cannot revoke admin. Operator-controlled; never sourced from a plugin. Sugar for `initial_grants` with role ['tap_admin']; boot folds the two into one effective grant map.

initial_grants.description: Verified email -> the human-assignable roles granted to that person on each login (req-tap-auth-boot), generalizing initial_admins beyond tap_admin. Add/update-only and idempotent — applied on login, never reconciles or revokes (a typo or de-listing cannot silently drop access; de-provisioning is a separate explicit action). The role enum is the HUMAN-assignable set only; program-actor roles (tap_bootloader, tap_cares.*) are not grantable to a person here — the load-bearing security edge. Operator-controlled; never sourced from a plugin.

additionalProperties.description: The roles granted to this email on login. Human-assignable roles only; held in sync with tap_auth.roles.HUMAN_ASSIGNABLE_ROLES by a guard test.

local_password_enabled.description: true (default): local Django password login is available (dev + recovery). false: password login is disabled everywhere including Django admin (req-tap-auth-local) — does NOT deactivate users or invalidate sessions. Customer profiles disable it once IdP login is ready.

allow_admin_lockout.description: Break-glass (req-tap-auth-boot last-admin invariant). false (default): boot fails loud if applying this profile would leave no active human tap_admin. true: a secure admin-lockout standup is permitted by design (recovery via the out-of-band management/shell floor). Satellite/headless only.
